note: Event cards typed by Orbis from the cited Wikipedia articles. Dates are Gregorian; cards marked Julian show the Julian date their sources use (England kept the Julian calendar until 1752).

items.title: Charles of Habsburg inherits Spain
items.text: Charles, grandson of Ferdinand and Isabella and of Emperor Maximilian, inherited Castile and Aragon, with Naples, Sicily and Sardinia. In 1519 he was also elected Holy Roman Emperor as Charles V.

items.title: Mohács: Hungary's king falls
items.text: Louis II of Hungary and Bohemia died fleeing the Ottoman army. Under a marriage treaty, his brother-in-law Ferdinand of Habsburg was elected king in both kingdoms.

items.title: Charles V divides his empire
items.text: Charles V abdicated: Spain, the Netherlands and the Italian lands went to his son Philip II, Austria and the imperial title to his brother Ferdinand. Two Habsburg lines ruled from then on.

items.title: Spain's king takes Portugal
items.text: After Portugal's king died without heirs, Philip II of Spain claimed the crown and won it by force. Portugal regained its own king, John IV of Braganza, in 1640.

items.title: Henry IV, the first Bourbon
items.text: The last Valois king, Henry III, was murdered; his distant cousin Henry of Navarre succeeded him. Bourbons ruled France until 1792 and again 1814-1848.

items.title: Michael Romanov elected tsar
items.text: After 15 years of famine, civil war and Polish occupation, an assembly in Moscow chose 16-year-old Michael Romanov as tsar. His family ruled until 1917.

items.title: Augustus of Saxony elected king of Poland
items.text: The Elector of Saxony, Frederick Augustus I, converted to Catholicism and won the election to the Polish throne as Augustus II. Saxon kings ruled Poland for most of 1697-1763.

items.title: War of the Spanish Succession
items.text: Charles II, the last Spanish Habsburg, left his crowns to Philip of Anjou, grandson of Louis XIV. Britain, Austria and the Dutch went to war to stop a Bourbon union of France and Spain.

items.title: A king in Prussia
items.text: Elector Frederick III of Brandenburg crowned himself Frederick I, King in Prussia, at Königsberg, today's Kaliningrad, outside the Holy Roman Empire.

items.title: Peace of Utrecht
items.text: Philip V kept Spain but gave up any claim to France. Austria took Spain's Netherlands, Milan, Naples and Sardinia; Savoy got Sicily, which it swapped for Sardinia in 1720.

items.title: Napoleon crowns himself emperor
items.text: In Notre-Dame, Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French. Within four years his brothers were kings of Naples, Holland, Westphalia and Spain.

items.title: A French marshal for Sweden
items.text: The childless Charles XIII needed an heir. Sweden's estates elected Napoleon's marshal Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte; he became king in 1818, and his descendants still reign.

items.title: Leopold I, king of the Belgians
items.text: After Belgium broke away from the Netherlands, Prince Leopold of Saxe-Coburg took the new throne. The Coburgs later also married into the thrones of Portugal and Britain and won Bulgaria's.

items.title: Kingdom of Italy
items.text: Victor Emmanuel II of Savoy, king of Sardinia, became king of Italy. Venice joined in 1866 and Rome in 1870.

items.title: A Danish prince for Greece
items.text: After Greece deposed the Bavarian Otto, its assembly elected the 17-year-old Danish prince William, who reigned as George I until 1913.

items.title: German Empire proclaimed
items.text: In the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, King Wilhelm I of Prussia was proclaimed German Emperor. Bavaria, Saxony and the other states kept their own kings and dukes inside the empire.

items.title: Haakon VII: Norway's own king
items.text: After Norway left its union with Sweden, it chose Prince Carl of Denmark as king; he took the name Haakon VII.

items.title: Empires fall
items.text: Defeat in the First World War ended Europe's great monarchies: Russia's in 1917, Germany's and Austria-Hungary's in November 1918, the Ottoman sultanate in 1922.

items.title: Italy votes for a republic
items.text: In a referendum, 54% of voters chose a republic; the Savoy king Umberto II left for exile in Portugal.

items.title: Juan Carlos restores the Spanish crown
items.text: Two days after Franco's death, Juan Carlos of Bourbon, Franco's chosen successor and grandson of the last king, was proclaimed king.
